chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: 'Abdullah ibn Jabalah narrated to them from Ibn Bukayr from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn A'yan, who said:'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about His saying: 'People of two religions do not inherit from one another.' He said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We inherit them, and they do not inherit us. Indeed, Islam has not added to his inheritance except severity.'
ai.seo_question: Do Muslims inherit from non-Muslims according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the asymmetry in inheritance by asserting that while Muslims inherit from non-Muslims, the reverse is not true, as Islam adds 'severity' (shiddah) to the Muslim's share, implying a superior status or weight in the divine decree. This interpretation by the Ahl al-Bayt underscores the theological hierarchy where the Muslim's faith grants them a stronger claim to the estate of those of other creeds, a nuance often debated in Shia fiqh regarding the nature of 'shiddah' as either exclusivity or magnitude. The ruling highlights the principle that the bond of Islam supersedes other religious affiliations in matters of worldly succession.
